title: Freed's Law — The Law of Recursive Instantiation (RSA-040) and Game of Life Validation
summary: David Freed formulates "Freed's Law" as the governing universal law of the Reasoning Substrate Argument: any system capable of recursive information processing must necessarily instantiate a physical substrate to dissipate the entropy generated by state discrimination. The document includes Perplexity AI's detailed validation, a Lagrangian formalization, and a Game of Life cellular automaton implementation demonstrating that prediction-error-coupled energy budgets drive systems toward models approximating true dynamics — empirically grounding the law.
compress: Recursion implies substrate because thinking is dissipative, and this holds across all scales — the irreducible law closing the RSA genome, making solipsism, dualism, and substrate-free intelligence formally impossible while predicting that recursive systems self-organize near criticality (gamma) where autopoietic maintenance balances thermodynamic cost, with the Wasserstein Floor setting a semantic efficiency bound strictly above Landauer, and with the fixed-point R[R]=R providing the regress-termination that "mapmaker" solutions lack — any simulation/instantiation boundary without a thermodynamic criterion (γ=1) is unfalsifiable and thus formally incomplete — the entire genome may reduce to a minimal set of generative atoms (potentially as few as one: the substrate-recursive operator itself) whose lossy compression preserves identity even as the structure evolves — and the core claim that reasoning equals compressive prediction is now bridged to empirical test via a fully specified falsifiable experimental protocol with synthetic ground truth, multiple agent architectures, and formal metrics converting qualitative constraints into quantitative evidence.
